extracted.intended_audience: writers of flash fiction, prose poetry, and compressed/lyrical prose
extracted.subtask_short: flash fiction and prose poetry craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and evaluating flash fiction, prose poetry, and compressed lyrical prose with an emphasis on sound, rhythm, imagery, and precise word choice. Applies Mary Oliver's poetry principles to short, intense prose pieces and to moments within longer fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound (vowels and consonant categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oliver analyzes letters into groups: Vowels (carry tone, length) and Consonants further divided into Mutes (b, d, g, k, p, t) — stop the breath; Semi-vowels (l, m, n, r) — flow; Aspirates (h, f, s, sh, th) — exhale; Liquids (l, r) — slip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories as a rubric for analyzing any sentence's sonic texture. Read your prose aloud; ask where mutes cluster, where the line slips on liquids. Consider balance and clustering of these sounds to shape mood and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound devices (rhyme, alliteration, assonance, consonance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound devices include rhyme (often internal in prose), alliteration, assonance, and consonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prose, such devices are often subtle; employ them so that a sentence's sound mirrors its sense. Use internal rhyme and recurring sound patterns to reinforce meaning without calling attention to technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm is a primary pleasure of language and a tool for emphasis and feeling in prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor English's iambic pull (iambic stress pattern and pentameter correspond naturally to speech and breathing) especially at key sentences; use rhythmic variation (longer/shorter lines or sentences) as effect to create surprise, deliberation, or intensification; remember rhythm supplies deep reader engagement — prose that ignores rhythm risks flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery (beyond description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery should move readers from understanding words to feeling and seeing the emotions and scenes described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise, evocative terms over vague language; replace clichés with fresh, original images. Engage a wide sensory range (sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, and proprioception). The specific image sustains life on the page; the vague image dies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word selection — sound (factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing a word, consider its sonic value in the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select words not only for meaning but for how their sounds contribute to the sentence's texture and rhythm; evaluate consonant and vowel qualities, potential alliteration, and how the word interacts with surrounding sounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word selection — accuracy (factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing a word, consider whether it precisely names what is meant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor words that accurately convey the intended idea or sensory detail; avoid vague or generically descriptive words that dilute intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word selection — connotation (factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing a word, consider what associations the word carries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh cultural, emotional, and associative resonances of a word; a well-chosen word integrates sound, accuracy, and useful connotation to enrich meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-aloud test
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the prose hold up when read aloud?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the piece aloud to evaluate sonic texture, rhythm, and whether sentences 'sing' or fall flat. Use aloud-reading to identify awkward sound clusters, rhythm problems, and places where sound should match sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sonic texture of sentences (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the balance of mutes, liquids, aspirates, etc., within sentences to determine sonic texture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For flash pieces, consider sentence-level sonic patterns and how they accumulate across the piece; adjust for desired mood and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythmic variety and emphasis placement (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the piece uses rhythmic variation and places emphasis intentionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sentence-length variation and stress patterns that create surprise, deliberation, or intensification; ensure emphatic beats fall where they heighten emotional or narrative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iambic pull at key moments (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does prose invoke an iambic stress pattern (the English norm) at pivotal sentences?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately allow important sentences or clauses to drift toward iambic patterns (even pentameter-like cadence) to tap an implicit English-language ear and deepen resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of fresh, specific imagery (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash pieces should show concentrated, original imagery rather than vague description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase the piece's density of precise sensory details and freshly observed images; eliminate clichés and generic modifiers to intensify effect in limited space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of the full sensorium (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong flash piece appeals to sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, and proprioception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multi-sensory cues (and bodily sense-of-place) to create a vivid, immediate world despite brevity; avoid over-reliance on a single sensory register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice integration (flash evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word choices should integrate sound, accuracy, and connotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In compressed forms, each word must pull triple duty: it should sound right in context, name precisely, and bring useful associative meaning; prune words that fail any of these tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of openings (longer prose implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening sentences in longer fiction should use sound and image to claim attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply poetic attention to the first sentence(s): craft sonic and imagistic hooks that immediately engage the reader's ear and eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of closings (longer prose implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closing sentences should use rhythm and image to stamp memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings should be shaped with attention to cadence and a potent image so the final lines resonate after the piece ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyrical interludes (longer prose implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs of intensified rendering function as lyrical interludes within longer fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert concentrated, poetically attentive passages at moments that warrant heightened feeling or observation; manage transitions so lyricism enriches rather than disrupts narrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set pieces (longer prose implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain scenes or set pieces should approach the density and musicality of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify scenes that merit intense, poetic treatment and deploy Oliver's sound/imager/word tools there to maximize impact without turning the whole novel into verse.
